claims.title: Independent public-seed convexification of a fixed-model policy frontier is an exact finite zero-sum game
claims.scope: finite exact active fixed-model root frontiers with a fixed modelwise benchmark vector and source-independent public mixing over complete deterministic policy trees
assumptions: expected modelwise costs are linear in the public-seed mixture
the root frontier is complete below configured caps
the exact rational game support search completes below its configured cap
nonclaims: the public seed is an explicit assistance resource
the theorem does not assert a polynomial-time solver
the result is not evidence for simulation

claims.title: Componentwise dominated deterministic policy trees are unnecessary after public-seed convexification
claims.scope: finite modelwise cost vectors under minimization of the worst expected coordinate after arbitrary public mixing
assumptions: a dominated policy has another available policy no worse in every model coordinate
mixture weights are source-independent
nonclaims: Pareto pruning does not bound the frontier size polynomially
the argument concerns expected cost vectors rather than arbitrary nonlinear policy statistics

claims.title: After matching public-randomness resources, restoring an experiment's observation information cannot worsen minimax benchmark gap
claims.scope: an actual finite experiment menu and its information-erased menu with identical experiment names and acquisition costs, both additionally convexified by the same independent public-seed resource
assumptions: an actual controller may ignore observations and emulate every information-erased deterministic policy
both policy classes are evaluated against the same fixed benchmark vector
the public seed can mix the same complete deterministic policies on both sides
nonclaims: information erasure changes observation alphabets while preserving declared acquisition cost

claims.title: The actual model-informed causal oracle is a valid fixed benchmark for information-erased policies
claims.scope: actual and information-erased versions of the same active experiment menu under one globally fixed model
assumptions: the actual singleton-model oracle may ignore its observations
actual and erased experiment menus have identical acquisition costs and causal timing
the oracle and shared policies use the same zero-error code universe
nonclaims: the fixed benchmark is one declared estimand rather than the only possible experiment-value definition

claims.title: Deterministic experiment gain has an exact coordination-information-residual-randomization decomposition
claims.scope: actual and information-erased active fixed-model policy classes evaluated against one fixed actual oracle vector, with deterministic and independently public-mixed values
assumptions: D0, M0, DA, and MA refer to the four declared policy classes under the same benchmark
all four exact finite optimizations complete
nonclaims: the three terms are operational resource values rather than ontological quantities
the residual randomization term is subtracted rather than asserted to be an additional positive component of deterministic gain

claims.title: Perfect K3 model revelation decomposes unit deterministic gain into one-third coordination and two-thirds information value
claims.scope: three one-state point-mass K3 models, one period, a free perfectly model-revealing experiment, and the actual model-informed oracle vector (1,1,1)
assumptions: complete binary prefix codes have state-length permutations of (1,2,2)
public mixing is free only in the mixed comparison classes
nonclaims: the one-third/two-thirds split is specific to this symmetric finite construction

claims.title: A source-independent public K3 coin has zero resource-matched information value
claims.scope: three one-state point-mass K3 models with a uniform three-way signal independent of model and source
assumptions: the information-erased mixed class and actual mixed class both admit an independent public seed
the fixed actual oracle vector is (1,1,1)
nonclaims: the public coin can still have positive coordination value under deterministic policies

claims.title: No-signal K3 has zero total experiment gain because erased coordination and actual residual-randomization gaps cancel
claims.scope: three one-state point-mass K3 models with a one-symbol no-signal experiment
assumptions: deterministic regret is one and public-mixed regret is two-thirds under the fixed actual oracle
nonclaims: the cancellation identity does not mean public randomness is valueless; it means the actual and erased experiment are the same information structure

claims.title: Bounded exact active-experiment regret-decomposition audit
claims.scope: perfect-revelation, source-independent public-coin, no-signal, noisy-signal, information-erasure, and exact primal-dual game checks exercised by repository tests
assumptions: all active policy frontier searches and singleton oracle solves complete below configured caps
all zero-sum support searches complete below configured caps
all probabilities and costs use exact rational arithmetic
nonclaims: bounded checks are not a continuous-model or scalability theorem
CI success is not empirical evidence for simulation
